terms.x: a place a future can pause
terms.p: An await inside an async function: the one kind of place where the task can give control back and be resumed later.

terms.x: what an async fn compiles into
terms.p: The enum the compiler builds from an async function, with one variant per await point holding exactly the variables that must survive it.

terms.x: the callback that says try again
terms.p: The handle a future gives to whatever it is waiting on, so that when the data arrives the executor is told to poll that task again.
The library component that holds a queue of tasks and polls them; Rust ships none, so you pick tokio or another runtime.

terms.x: a promise not to move a value
terms.p: A wrapper saying the value behind it will stay at one address forever, which is what makes it safe for a future to hold a pointer into itself.
The problem that async code can call ordinary code but not the reverse, so making one function async tends to force every caller to become async too.
The two-variant enum a future's poll method returns: Ready with the final value, or Pending meaning ask again after the waker fires.
